requirements.title: Asynchronous transfer without an immediate status condition initiates a pending operation
requirements.definition: Execution of an asynchronous data transfer statement in which no error, end-of-record, or end-of-file condition occurs initiates a pending data transfer operation.

pending.async-transfer-initiates-pending-operati: Use a future asynchronous named-file transfer with ID= into an initialized status variable; after the transfer begins, perform a WAIT on that ID and verify the transferred value from nondefault sentinels, not timing.

requirements.definition: A pending data transfer operation remains pending until a corresponding wait operation is performed.

requirements.title: Each wait operation completes processing for only one data transfer operation
requirements.definition: A wait operation completes the processing of a pending data transfer operation, and each wait operation completes only a single data transfer operation.

pending.wait-completes-processing: Initiate a pending asynchronous transfer into nondefault storage, WAIT for it, and assert the resulting data/status after WAIT.
pending.wait-completes-only-single-operation: Initiate two pending transfers with distinct IDs and sentinel targets; WAIT for one ID and then separately WAIT for the other before asserting both values, avoiding any claim that one ID wait completed both.

requirements.title: A wait operation waits for incomplete transfer and defines successful input storage
requirements.definition: If the actual data transfer is not yet complete, the wait operation first waits for completion; if a pending input operation completes without error, the storage units of the input/output storage sequence become defined with the transferred values.

pending.wait-waits-for-actual-completion: Use a pending asynchronous input with the target prefilled by nondefault sentinels and perform WAIT before reading the target; the oracle is the post-WAIT value, not elapsed time.
pending.successful-input-wait-defines-storage-va: Read known records asynchronously into sentinel storage and after successful WAIT assert the exact values described by the registered data-transfer rules.

requirements.title: Wait-operation status conditions take the wait statement specifier actions
requirements.definition: If an error, end-of-file, or end-of-record condition occurs during a wait operation, the applicable IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, ERR=, END=, and EOR= actions of the statement performing the wait operation are taken.

pending.wait-error-actions: Use only a future status condition attributable to another registered rule; initialize IOSTAT and a labelled branch sentinel, then assert nonzero/named status or branch selection, never IOMSG text.
pending.wait-end-actions: Create a named file with a known end condition and a pending asynchronous READ; WAIT with END= and IOSTAT initialized to sentinels and assert only the portable end status/branch.
pending.wait-eor-actions: Use nonadvancing asynchronous input that reaches EOR; WAIT with EOR= and sentinel status/branch variables, asserting only the portable EOR outcome.

requirements.title: An error or end-of-file during a unit wait causes waits for all pending transfers on that unit
requirements.definition: If an error or end-of-file condition occurs during a wait operation for a unit, the processor performs a wait operation for all pending data transfer operations for that unit.

requirements.title: Completed wait operations leave the operation and storage sequence no longer pending
requirements.definition: After completion of the wait operation, the data transfer operation and its input/output storage sequence are no longer considered pending.

pending.operation-no-longer-pending-after-wait: After a WAIT for a specific ID, a second WAIT for all operations on the same unit should have no remaining operation to complete; assert no additional data change beyond the established result.
pending.storage-sequence-no-longer-pending-after: After WAIT, use the formerly pending input storage in an ordinary comparison against the known transferred value; the pre-WAIT sentinel establishes non-vacuity.

accounting.rationale: Pending-operation initiation, permissions, duration, and statement-set admission are split.
Asynchronous transfer initiates a pending operation.
Pending duration is fixed until a corresponding wait.
Defines the statements that can perform wait operations.
Single-operation completion and single-statement multiple-wait permission are split.
A wait completes processing for only one operation.
A statement may perform multiple waits.
Waits for actual completion and defines successful input storage.
Status conditions during wait take the wait statement actions.
Error or EOF during wait causes waits for all pending operations for the unit.
NOTE explains possible timing of asynchronous status conditions; not normative.
Completion makes the operation and storage sequence no longer pending.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.5-12.9: termination of data transfer, WAIT, BACKSPACE, ENDFILE, REWIND and FLUSH (batch164). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found the portable WAIT no-operation cases missing - WAIT with ID=0 (explicitly permitted by 12.7.2 p3) and with ID= omitted on an asynchronous connection with nothing pending must succeed with IOSTAT zero - and an ENDFILE position plan that used REWIND, destroying the state under test; ENDFILE is now observed by the BACKSPACE that 12.8.3 p2 requires before the next transfer, after which a READ must report IOSTAT_END. Seventeen numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
